scores.label: A
scores.note: No judged option is labelled 0. Options 5 (echo) and 10 (duplicate) failed the code checks and were not judged. The first three options are plain near-synonyms, and the stronger picks (nervous, apprehensive, timid) come later in the list.

scores.label: B
scores.note: Option 3 'alarmed' is 0: it means suddenly startled by an event, not a lasting fear of speaking. Option 8 'humbly' is 0: it is an adverb and ungrammatical after 'too'. Option 10 'caught' is 0: it is the wrong sense and makes no sense in the sentence.

scores.label: C
scores.note: No option is labelled 0. 'Uncomfortable', 'hesitant' and 'insecure' drift slightly away from fear but still suit the paragraph. 'Intimidated' and 'timid' are strong fits.

scores.label: D
scores.note: Option 8 'distrustful' is 0: it changes the meaning from fear to suspicion of others. Option 10 'reluctant' is 0: 'too reluctant to talk' is unidiomatic and loses the fear. 'Terrified' overstates the feeling.

scores.label: E
scores.note: Option 5 'dreadful' is 0: it is the wrong sense (it means terrible, not afraid). Option 7 'panic-stricken' is 0: it badly overstates a lasting state that held 'most of the time'. 'Terrified' also overstates.
